adjudication.evidence: P1 (528–560) shows a sustained offset in N/E/U with onset ~+3.4/-1.3/-0.8, but interior observations (e.g., indices 542–546) show a sharp, independent step of ~−7.7/−13.7/−8.6 (P2), inconsistent with a smooth return; P2 is too short and isolated to be a genuine temporary platform—its magnitude dwarfs surrounding motion and lacks opposing return. The large jump at index 543 (nuisance_step_days) coincides with P2 and disrupts continuity of P1. No sustained opposing return across same axes is observed for either candidate; physical motion continues smoothly before/after, but the interval contains an independent permanent step, not a closed temporary offset. Thus, neither P1 nor P2 qualifies as a genuine temporary platform.
